title: Coupon applied twice at checkout, and any customer could download another customer's invoice
summary:
Two defects were found while the checkout and order-history pages were tested before release. Both are fixed on this branch.

When a shopper refreshed the cart page, the coupon was applied a second time, so 1,240 orders in the test run were charged too little (USD 3,180 in total). Separately, the invoice download link accepted any order number: a logged-in shopper could change the number in the address bar and download someone else's invoice, with their name, address and items.

The coupon is now calculated once from the cart subtotal and stored with the order, and every invoice is loaded only through the signed-in customer's own orders. New tests cover both rules, and a person repeated the checks by hand with two separate customer accounts.

problems.title: Coupon discount applied twice when the cart is refreshed
problems.symptom: A 10% coupon on a USD 50.00 cart gave a total of USD 40.50 instead of USD 45.00 after the page was refreshed once.
problems.root_cause: `applyCoupon()` took the discount off the current cart total instead of the original subtotal, and it ran again on every cart refresh. Nothing recorded that the coupon was already applied.
problems.impact: In the staging test run, 1,240 of 9,800 orders were under-charged, USD 3,180 in total. In production this would be lost revenue and manual refunds or re-billing.
problems.evidence:
Test order SF-20261029-0417: subtotal 50.00, coupon SAVE10, charged 40.50.
The cart log shows `applyCoupon` called twice for the same cart within 4 seconds.

problems.title: Invoice download did not check who owns the order
problems.symptom: Signed in as test customer A, opening `/api/orders/1002/invoice` downloaded the invoice of customer B.
problems.root_cause: The route loaded the order with `Order.findById(req.params.id)` and only checked that someone was signed in, not that the order belonged to them. Order numbers are sequential, so they are easy to guess.
problems.impact: Any customer could read other customers' names, addresses, phone numbers and purchases: a personal-data leak that would have to be reported in many countries.
problems.evidence: Request as customer A (id 77) for order 1002 (owned by customer 81) returned HTTP 200 with the PDF.

fixes.title: Calculate the coupon once, from the subtotal
fixes.change: The discount is now calculated from `cart.subtotal`, and the applied coupon is stored on the cart. Applying the same coupon again changes nothing. A unique index on (cart_id, coupon_code) blocks duplicates at database level.
fixes.why_correct: The total no longer depends on how many times the page loads, and the database refuses a second copy even if two requests arrive together.

fixes.title: Load invoices only through the customer's own orders
fixes.change: The route now looks the order up with both the order id and the signed-in customer's id, and answers 404 when it does not match.
fixes.why_correct: A customer can only reach orders that belong to them. The 404 response does not reveal whether another customer's order exists.

fixes.title: Tests for both rules
fixes.change: Added tests: refreshing the cart three times keeps one discount; customer A gets 404 for customer B's invoice and 200 for their own.
fixes.why_correct: Both tests failed on the old code and pass on the new code, so they guard against the same defect coming back.

verification.detail: 214 tests, 0 failures; the 2 new tests failed before the fix.
No HIGH or WARN findings left; 2 INFO about outbound calls, both expected.
Every function, import and route used in the change exists.

verification.check: Manual test with two customer accounts
verification.detail: Customer A could not open customer B's invoice; both could open their own.

verification.check: Checkout refreshed 5 times with a coupon
verification.detail: Total stayed at USD 45.00 on a USD 50.00 cart with SAVE10.

verification.check: Code read by a second developer
verification.detail: Approved, with one note: rename `invoicePath` to `invoiceFilePath` later.

scans.note: The HIGH before the fix was the invoice route reading an order by an id from the request without an ownership check.

approvals.action: Run the new migration on the local database
approvals.harm: Adds a unique index; fails if duplicate rows already exist

approvals.action: Run the same migration on the shared staging database
approvals.harm: Locks the carts table for a few seconds; other testers see the change at once

remaining_risks: Orders already charged too little in staging must be corrected before the data is copied anywhere else.
Other download routes (receipts, shipping labels) use the same pattern and have not been checked yet.
next_steps: Run the migration on staging during the quiet hour, as agreed.
Review the receipts and shipping-label routes for the same ownership check.
Run the checkout load test before release.
